n: Jesus explains why he is warning them in advance: so they won’t stumble and fall away when persecution comes.

f.g: offended = caused to stumble, to lose faith.

n: They will be thrown out of synagogues, and some who kill them will even think they are serving God. Saul of Tarsus would be one such persecutor before his conversion.

f.w: put you out of the synagogues
will think that he doeth God service

n: Persecutors act this way because they don’t truly know the Father or the Son.

f.w: they have not known the Father

n: He tells them now so they will remember his warning when it happens. He hadn’t mentioned it earlier because he was with them to protect them.

f.w: ye may remember that I told you

n: He is returning to the Father who sent him, yet none of them are asking where he’s going — they’re focused on their own loss.

f.g: Peter and Thomas had asked earlier (13:36; 14:5), but now grief has silenced them.

n: Because of what he has told them, sorrow has filled their hearts.
Still, it is for their good that he leaves, for only then will the Comforter come. The Holy Ghost could be a constant companion to every disciple everywhere.

f.w: It is expedient for you that I go away

n: When the Comforter comes, he will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment — showing people the truth about themselves and about Christ.
Concerning sin: the deepest sin is refusing to believe in Christ.
Concerning righteousness: Jesus’s return to the Father vindicates him as the Righteous One, even though the world condemned him.
Concerning judgment: Satan, the ruler of this world, has already been judged and defeated by Christ’s victory.

f.w: the prince of this world is judged

n: There is much more he could teach, but they cannot handle it yet. Revelation comes line upon line, as we are ready.
The Spirit of truth will guide them into all truth. He won’t speak on his own but will speak what he hears, and will reveal things to come.

f.w: he will guide you into all truth
he will shew you things to come

n: The Spirit will glorify Jesus by taking what is his and making it known to them. The Holy Ghost always points to Christ.
Everything the Father has belongs to the Son too, so what the Spirit reveals from the Son comes from the Father as well. Father, Son, and Holy Ghost work in perfect unity.

f.w: All things that the Father hath are mine

n: In a little while they won’t see him (at his death), and then in a little while they will see him again (at his resurrection).
Some disciples puzzle among themselves over his words about “a little while” and going to the Father.

f.w: What is this that he saith unto us
f.g: Their repeated confusion is honest and relatable.

n: They keep repeating the phrase, admitting they don’t understand.

f.w: we cannot tell what he saith

n: Jesus senses they want to ask and raises the question for them.

f.w: Jesus knew that they were desirous to ask him

n: They will weep and mourn while the world celebrates his death, but their grief will be turned into joy.

f.w: your sorrow shall be turned into joy

n: Like a woman in labor, whose pain is forgotten in the joy of her newborn, their anguish will give way to joy when new life comes.
They are sorrowful now, but he will see them again, their hearts will rejoice, and no one will be able to take that joy away.

f.w: your joy no man taketh from you

n: In that day they won’t need to ask him questions as before; they may pray directly to the Father in Jesus’s name, and the Father will give it. This is why we pray to the Father in Christ’s name.

f.w: Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name

n: Until now they haven’t prayed in his name. Now they should ask and receive, so their joy may be full.
He has been using figures of speech, but the time is coming when he will speak plainly about the Father.

f.g: proverbs = figures of speech, veiled sayings.

n: In that day they will ask in his name. Jesus does not mean he stops interceding, but that they will have direct access to the Father.

f.w: I will pray the Father for you

n: The Father himself loves them because they have loved Jesus and believed he came from God.
Jesus summarizes his whole mission in one sentence: he came from the Father into the world, and now leaves the world to return to the Father.

f.w: I came forth from the Father

n: The disciples say that now he is speaking plainly, not in figures.
They declare their confidence that he knows all things and that he came from God.
Jesus asks, perhaps with gentle irony, “Do you believe now?” Their faith is real but about to be tested.

f.g: Could also be read as a statement: “Now you believe” — yet trials are coming.

n: The hour has come when they will scatter and leave him alone. Yet he is not alone, because the Father is with him.
His final word before his prayer: in him they can have peace. The world will bring troubles, but take heart — he has overcome the world.
